title: Trade event listener
context: Consumes executed trades from Kafka, updates the user's position, and publishes a position-updated event that the portfolio screen listens to.

points.title: Not idempotent
points.why: Kafka delivers at least once. A redelivered trade (after a rebalance, or a crash before the offset commit) is added to the position twice.
points.fix: Store processed trade ids (with a unique constraint) in the same transaction and skip duplicates.

points.title: Dual write: DB and Kafka aren't atomic
points.why: The send isn't part of the DB transaction. The event can go out and the DB then roll back, or the DB commits and the send is lost.
points.fix: Use a transactional outbox: write the event to a table in the same transaction and relay it to Kafka.

points.title: Crash on a user's first trade in a ticker

why.java: No position exists yet, so findBy… returns null and the next line throws a NullPointerException. The message is then retried forever.
why.kotlin: No position exists yet, so findBy… returns null and !! throws. The message is then retried forever.

points.fix: Create a new position when none exists (and add a unique constraint on user and ticker).

points.title: Poison message blocks the partition
points.why: Malformed JSON throws on every retry, so the consumer is stuck on that offset and every later trade in the partition waits.
points.fix: Configure a DefaultErrorHandler with limited retries and a dead-letter topic; use ErrorHandlingDeserializer.

points.title: Concurrent updates can overwrite each other
points.why: If two consumers update the same position (for example after repartitioning), one update is lost.
points.fix: Key trade messages by user id so ordering is per user, and add @Version optimistic locking.

points.title: Hand-made ObjectMapper

why.java: It skips Spring's configured mapper (JavaTimeModule, naming rules), so dates and fields serialise differently from the rest of the app.
why.kotlin: It skips Spring's configured mapper. Without jackson-module-kotlin it can't even build Kotlin data classes, and dates serialise differently from the rest of the app.

points.fix: Inject the ObjectMapper bean Spring Boot configures.

points.title: JPA entity used as the event contract
points.why: Any change to the entity silently breaks consumers, and lazy fields can fail to serialise.
points.fix: Publish an explicit, versioned event DTO.
